pull_requests.title: feat(openfeature): add immediate experimentation opt-out
pull_requests.body:
### Motivation

Applications need to stop a subject's experiment participation without disabling ordinary feature delivery. Evaluation telemetry remains a separate control.

### What does this PR do?

- Add `DD_FEATURE_FLAGS_EXPERIMENTATION_OPT_OUT_MODE=disabled|immediate`. The default is `disabled`.
- Resolve the mode at provider construction. Explicit `ProviderConfig.ExperimentationOptOutMode` overrides SDK configuration. Unsupported values return a construction error.
- Read the optional `dd_experimentation_opt_out_at` RFC3339 timestamp on each evaluation. Invalid input returns `INVALID_CONTEXT` and the application default, including for ordinary flags. The error explains how to correct the timestamp or omit the attribute. Parsing follows allocation `startAt` and `endAt`.
- Skip allocations with `doLog=true` or omitted before targeting and randomization. Continue through ordinary allocations, or return the application default.
- Preserve eligible assignments. Store no preference history and emit no withdrawal events.
- Pin the merged [shared fixtures #49](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/pull/49) and run its capability cases through the existing reader.

Holdouts and winner rollouts with `doLog=true` are also excluded. Ordinary delivery requires a matching `doLog=false` allocation. Immediate withdrawal can affect experiment analysis.

The setting is registered in the [central configuration registry](https://feature-parity.us1.prod.dog/#/configurations?viewType=configurations&configKey=3392).

Set the environment variable before SDK initialization:

```sh
export DD_FEATURE_FLAGS_EXPERIMENTATION_OPT_OUT_MODE=immediate
```

```go
import (
    "time"

    ddflags "github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/v2/openfeature"
    of "github.com/open-feature/go-sdk/openfeature"
)

// At startup, after the Datadog tracer starts:
provider, err := ddflags.NewDatadogProvider(ddflags.ProviderConfig{})
if err != nil {
    return err
}
if err := of.SetNamedProviderAndWait("my-app", provider); err != nil {
    return err
}
client := of.NewClient("my-app")

// In each request handler, OptOutAt is a customer-owned *time.Time.
attributes := map[string]any{}
if user.OptOutAt != nil {
    attributes["dd_experimentation_opt_out_at"] =
        user.OptOutAt.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339Nano)
}
enabled, err := client.BooleanValue(
    ctx, "new-feature", false,
    of.NewEvaluationContext(user.ID, attributes),
)
```

A valid timestamp takes effect immediately, even when it is in the future. Omit the attribute to allow experimentation again.
Programmatic overrides use `ddflags.ExperimentationOptOutDisabled` or `ddflags.ExperimentationOptOutImmediate`.

A malformed value now returns `INVALID_CONTEXT` and the default for every flag, including flags with no experiments, so one bad attribute breaks ordinary delivery for that user. I suggest treating a malformed value as opted out: skip exposure-logging allocations, keep ordinary delivery, and log the problem once. inline_comments.body:
Yes I want to return `INVALID_CONTEXT` here only when they have enabled one of the opt out modes. My thinking is to give users immediate feedback that something is wrong, for a situation they have agreed to.

I want to keep strict timestamp validation. When a customer enables this mode, malformed input should produce clear, actionable feedback rather than us guessing their intent.

Immediate mode technically only needs an opt-out signal. However, the API accepts a timestamp, and I want that contract to remain consistent if we add future-experiments-only mode.

Invalid input therefore returns INVALID_CONTEXT and the application default, including for ordinary flags. I understand the delivery tradeoff. Customers can correct the timestamp or omit the attribute to allow participation.

I've added explicit documentation and tests for this behavior, plus an error message that explains how to correct the input.

**Release dependency (should fix before anyone turns on `immediate`):** an opted-out subject receives a shipped feature only if the winner's allocation has `doLog=false`. pull_requests.title: feat(openfeature): support opt-out from future experiments
pull_requests.body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds `ExperimentationOptOutFutureExperimentsOnly` and the environment value `future_experiments_only`.

For a subject with `dd_experimentation_opt_out_at`, compare the cutoff with each exposure-logging allocation's `randomizationActivatedAt`:

| Allocation activation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Before the cutoff | Continue normal evaluation and exposure logging. |
| At or after the cutoff, or unknown | Skip the allocation and continue ordinary delivery. |

Ordinary allocations remain eligible. Missing subject input preserves normal evaluation. Malformed subject input returns `INVALID_CONTEXT`, as in immediate mode. No new telemetry or subject history is added.

```sh
DD_FEATURE_FLAGS_EXPERIMENTATION_OPT_OUT_MODE=future_experiments_only
```

```go
// ProviderConfig{} uses the environment setting.
provider, err := ddflags.NewDatadogProvider(ddflags.ProviderConfig{})
if err != nil {
    return err
}
if err := of.SetNamedProviderAndWait("flags", provider); err != nil {
    return err
}
client := of.NewClient("flags")
attributes := map[string]any{}
if subject.ExperimentationOptOutAt != nil {
    attributes["dd_experimentation_opt_out_at"] =
        subject.ExperimentationOptOutAt.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339Nano)
}
enabled, err := client.BooleanValue(ctx, "new-route-planner", false,
    of.NewEvaluationContext(subject.ID, attributes))
```

An explicit `ProviderConfig{ExperimentationOptOutMode: ddflags.ExperimentationOptOutFutureExperimentsOnly}` overrides the environment setting.

### Motivation

Customers can stop new experiment participation while continuing older experiments. The cutoff describes allocation activation, not previous subject enrollment. An older experiment can still assign a subject for the first time.

**Stack:** #5666 supplies immediate mode and the configuration API. This PR adds the activation comparison. [Shared fixtures #52](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/pull/52) defines 42 capability checks; update the pin after that PR merges.

Enablement depends on the backend emitting stable activation metadata and retaining ordinary fallbacks. This PR does not deploy those changes. Allocations without metadata are skipped for opted-out subjects.

### Test coverage

Shared fixtures cover cutoff boundaries, timezone offsets, fractional seconds, invalid input, missing metadata, and fallback delivery. Local tests cover malformed activation metadata and valid-neighbor isolation in all modes, refresh, exposure deduplication, telemetry independence, and concurrent randomized subjects. Baseline and immediate-mode behavior remain covered. A benchmark covers all three modes.

[System tests #8135](https://github.com/DataDog/system-tests/pull/8135), stacked on system-tests #8080, add Remote Config, holdout assignment, exposure, and telemetry checks across all three modes. Release gating remains provisional until supported SDK releases are known.

Linux/amd64; `system-tests@6418472371431d01fbdb26cd220b90cd04077aa9`. | 12 passed; 0 failed; 0 skipped. |
